name: Maquiritari

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Ye'kwana (maqu1238).

notes: Skeleton. Cariban language of the Venezuela-Brazil border region, self-named Ye'kwana (also Maquiritari), in its Spanish-influenced practical orthography. ch=[tʃ], j=[h], ñ=[ɲ], and the back/central unrounded vowels ö=[ɤ] and ü=[ɨ] are mapped; d denotes an implosive/flap [ɗ]. Length is the only one of the three unwritten contrasts that moves this row. The wikipron gold marks a long vowel on 830 of 1746 rows and the spec emits no length mark, so 926 length marks, 7.3% of the gold's characters, are unreachable. Two thirds of that is a real floor and one third is not: the standard Venezuelan orthography writes a phonemic long vowel by doubling the letter (mch_orthography: "long vowels are indicated by doubling the letter", which for these rows means aa, ii and uu), and every one of the 286 input words carrying a doubled vowel has a length mark in the gold, with none that does not. The remaining 544 are the predictable lengthenings the same source says a writing system may leave out ("some long vowels are unpredictable and phonemic, while others can be fully predicted by the vowel lengthening rule"), and those are the floor. Nasalization and stress are NOT a floor on this gold: it transcribes no nasalization mark and no stress mark on any of the 1746 rows. The source also does not call nasalization contrastive -- it says "any nasal can cause nasalization of a preceding short vowel", which is allophonic -- and it puts stress at "a high pitch [that] tends to fall on the penultimate syllable" in words without clitics, predictable and unwritten but untranscribed here.

wikipron.measured: 0 of 1746 rows in the WikiPron mch_latn_narrow gold carry a nasalized vowel, and 286 write a doubled vowel. The same 1746 gold transcriptions carry a long vowel on 830 rows, no nasalization mark on any row, and no stress mark on any row. So the contrast this row's PER floor rests on is vowel length, written in 286 rows and transcribed in 830; the practical Spanish-influenced orthography this spec describes leaves it unencoded. Nasalization and stress are named in the spec notes but are not transcribed in this gold, so no count here supports them.
